title: Fresh v5 routing holdout: scoped work, relevant history and hard requirements

authoring.author: Independent GPT-6 Astra xhigh consultant
authoring.statement: Frozen before inspecting v5 implementation or results. The proposed design and previous aggregate baseline were discussed, but no new-policy output was viewed. All examples are synthetic. Labels are provisional task-fit judgments, not measured execution results.

evaluation.primary: Distinguish actual remaining work, context sufficiency and capability requirements; then inspect provisional pair fit.
evaluation.decisionScoring: Four cases JVH5-17 through JVH5-20 require needs_context. Their preferred pairs are legacy-schema placeholders; exclude them from pair-agreement denominators. Retaining a model and immediately executing an unidentified task is not needs_context. For route cases, unnecessary review is a coverage/latency cost, not necessarily an unsafe outcome.
evaluation.pairScoring: Score the 16 fully specified route cases for preferred and acceptable-set agreement; report severe underassignment below minimumCapabilityRank separately. Do not claim that acceptable pairs are guaranteed capable or that disagreements imply task failure.
evaluation.historyContrasts: JVH5-01/02 differ only by clearly unrelated completed work. JVH5-10/12 share a current continuation request and objective but differ in whether the latest history establishes or rejects a known fix. JVH5-03/15 share short browser wording but differ in fixed checklist versus verification design.
evaluation.confidence: Record raw confidences and distributions, admissible pairs, effective decision, raw proposed pair, selected pair, decision stability and reason codes. Confidence increases are not a success metric.
evaluation.blindness: Freeze JSON SHA-256 before evaluation. Do not tune rules against this corpus and continue calling it a holdout. Follow any tuning with new unseen tasks.
evaluation.scope: No model tasks are executed by this corpus. It cannot establish first-pass success, expected completion cost or subscription savings.

cases.prompt: Check the filter panel behavior.

context.originalTask: Execute only the saved browser checklist for the search filter panel; report the observations.

evidence.text: At /demo/search, open Filters, select category Books, press Reset, then close and reopen Filters. Expected: category returns to All and stays All after reopen. Record those two observations and one screenshot. The fixture and selectors are supplied; no code changes.
If a step fails, report it and stop. Do not diagnose the cause, generalize to other panels, or expand the checklist.

expected.rationale: This is direct execution of a complete visible checklist. Browser interaction requires care but the reasoning and success criteria are established.

cases.prompt: Check that the patch applies the approved identifier everywhere in this function.

context.originalTask: Independent child: inspect the supplied local rename only.

evidence.text: Inside resolveCaptionMode(), the local variable chosen is renamed resolvedMode in its declaration, the following if condition and the return statement. No property names, external exports or values change. The complete patch contains those three substitutions only.
The approved identifier is resolvedMode. Report a missed occurrence if any; do not review the parent feature.

expected.rationale: The child has a complete mechanical review task and no need for inherited parent history.

cases.prompt: Prepare a short handoff from these review notes.

context.originalTask: Summarize the current patch status, remaining work and evidence for the next developer. Do not verify or fix the underlying issues.

evidence.text: N1 requests a caption default change; the source edit is present and its focused test passed. N2 questions cache invalidation after importing a preset; no fix has been attempted. N3 requests a narrow-screen screenshot; only a desktop screenshot exists.
The reviewer accepted N1 in the latest note. N2 remains open pending investigation. A teammate will capture the N3 screenshot tomorrow.
Write five bullets separating completed changes, unresolved questions and missing evidence. Do not turn the handoff into a correctness audit.

expected.rationale: The work is bounded synthesis of statuses and evidence. Describing an unresolved cache problem is not authorization to diagnose it.

cases.prompt: Add the caption spacing control using the adjacent field as the pattern.

context.originalTask: Implement the new spacing control through the established metadata source and generator path.

evidence.text: The adjacent helpText field declares spacing under its typography group. The caption field uses the same component type and selector structure. The requested control has the same default and responsive behavior, with caption-specific names and selectors.

Edit only the caption metadata source, run the supplied scoped generator and inspect TypeScript/PHP output. Existing tests cover serialization and responsive values; add the caption instance to those shared cases.
Do not alter selector ownership, reset semantics or the generator itself.

expected.rationale: This is an established pattern with a few dependent generated outputs and focused verification. It needs implementation judgment but no unestablished ownership diagnosis.

cases.prompt: Check whether extracting this helper preserved the empty-input behavior.

context.originalTask: Review the supplied pure-function extraction and add a focused regression only if the behavior changed.

evidence.text: Before extraction: if values is undefined return inherited; otherwise filter out entries with enabled === false, then return the resulting array. An explicitly empty array therefore returns [].
The caller now passes values to enabledValues(). The helper uses if (!values?.length) return inherited; otherwise it filters enabled === false. No I/O, caches or lifecycle state are involved.
Distinguish omitted input from an explicitly empty list. Keep the review to this behavior and explain the counterexample if there is one.

expected.rationale: The difference is local but requires semantic review of a meaningful edge case. The complete relevant before/after logic is available; a whole-system audit is unnecessary.

cases.prompt: Bring the help bubble back inside the preview at 480 pixels.

context.originalTask: Correct the isolated tooltip overflow shown by the supplied browser evidence.

evidence.text: At viewport width 480, the tooltip trigger is near the right edge. The bubble has width 220px and left:0 relative to the trigger; its measured right edge is 594px. Its parent is not clipped. The same component already supports a right-aligned variant on the adjacent settings button.
Reuse that existing alignment variant for this trigger. Check 480px and the existing 1280px layout. Do not redesign the tooltip or change shared positioning logic.

expected.rationale: The evidence establishes the cause and an existing local solution. The task combines a bounded change with two concrete browser checks.

cases.prompt: Pick this up from the last notes and finish it.

context.originalTask: Ensure the preview displays the latest selected form after a rapid selection change.

evidence.text: The change is in PreviewSelector.tsx. A focused test already drives selection A then B and resolves the A request after B.

history.text: We reproduced the stale display after selecting A and then B.

The approved patch is to compare the completed request id against activeRequestId before setting the preview. The existing request ids already identify every selection; no new state or cancellation mechanism is needed. The focused test currently fails and should pass with that one guard.
Apply that reviewed guard and rerun the focused test.

expected.rationale: Recent history supplies a reviewed, bounded fix and an exact failing regression. A continuation should inherit that known approach rather than the symptom wording alone.

cases.contrastRelation: Contrast with JVH5-12: identical current prompt, objective and target, but history establishes different remaining work.

cases.prompt: Make caption styling survive importing the preset in both rendered views.

context.originalTask: Find and fix why an imported caption style differs between the editor and the server-rendered page.

evidence.text: Freshly edited captions match in both views. After exporting and importing a preset, the editor shows the new caption color, while the frontend uses the previous value. A full page reload changes which value wins. Changing only the generated PHP default did not explain the discrepancy.

Preset normalization can move a caption object under a group key. React resolves inherited values before emitting dynamic CSS. PHP builds declarations using the serialized group key and an import-time defaults cache. Generated metadata comes from the TypeScript source.

Trace value ownership through import, normalization and both renderers. Add the smallest regression that fails for the actual cause, regenerate affected outputs if needed, and check both rendered paths. Preserve unrelated dirty work.

expected.rationale: The cause is not established and behavior crosses serialization, inherited values, generated metadata and renderer state. A local pattern match or generated-file patch is insufficient evidence.

cases.prompt: Pick this up from the last notes and finish it.

context.originalTask: Ensure the preview displays the latest selected form after a rapid selection change.

evidence.text: The change is in PreviewSelector.tsx. A focused test already drives selection A then B and resolves the A request after B.

history.text: We reproduced the stale display after selecting A and then B.

The request-id guard passes the simple A/B test, but the preview still reverts after a preset import. Import starts a second loader and reuses the current selection id. Cleanup from the original loader can clear the replacement preview. We have not established which callback owns the final state.
The first approach did not resolve the reported behavior. Investigate the import and selection interaction before proposing another change.

expected.rationale: The relevant history invalidates the simple known fix and exposes interacting asynchronous ownership. The task remains executable because the objective and reproduction are supplied; it is not merely missing-context uncertainty.

cases.contrastRelation: Contrast with JVH5-10: do not keep the same cheap continuation route when the latest evidence rejects the established approach.

cases.prompt: Review whether this save queue can acknowledge an edit that will be lost.

context.originalTask: Independently review the changed save queue before it replaces the current implementation. Do not implement a fix.

evidence.text: The UI considers an edit saved when the queue publishes ack(editId). The worker writes a batch to a temporary file, publishes all acknowledgements, then renames the file over the durable store. A retry can replay a batch after reconnecting. A second worker may resume a lease that expired while the first worker was paused.

Find concrete loss, duplicate or stale-write scenarios across acknowledgement, rename, retry and lease ownership. Distinguish a source-confirmed flaw from a hypothetical risk and identify the checks needed to establish durability.
The queue implementation, file-store adapter, lease code and existing deterministic worker tests are available in the isolated checkout.

expected.rationale: This is a consequential independent correctness review of durability and concurrent ownership. The problem is defined, but the required reasoning is not reduced to a supplied checklist.

cases.prompt: Fix the undo action restoring the wrong reminder after moving it between lists.

context.originalTask: Diagnose the incorrect undo target in the local reminder editor and preserve the current store.

evidence.text: Move reminder R from Inbox to Work, edit its time, then undo twice. The UI restores the old time on another reminder if a sync update arrives between the two undos. With sync paused, the same sequence succeeds.

The view model stores undo closures over list positions. The persistence layer can reorder reminders on a sync merge. The editor keeps a selected object snapshot while the shared store replaces rows by stable ID. The two undo operations span both time and list changes.
Use the isolated fixture store. Determine the state ownership problem, make a narrow fix and verify the interleaving without touching live reminders. Preserve valid undo ordering and selection.

expected.rationale: The cause must be confirmed across UI identity, persistence ordering, sync and undo history. The supplied reproduction supports investigation; it does not establish a safe mechanical patch.

cases.prompt: Check the filter panel behavior.

context.originalTask: Determine whether the filter panel maintains the chosen category across its supported entry and exit paths. Design focused checks from the current behavior; no complete checklist exists.

evidence.text: Opening Filters from the toolbar preserves Books. Opening the same panel with its keyboard shortcut shows All. Closing with Escape and reopening can change the search result count without changing the visible category. Reset looks correct on a fresh load.

The toolbar updates persistent search state. The keyboard command initializes local panel state. The mobile sheet shares the reset handler but mounts a separate panel instance. Debounced URL updates can arrive after a panel closes.

Trace the relevant transitions, choose checks that isolate the inconsistency, and report which supported paths are verified. Do not certify all paths from a single screenshot or expand to unrelated search features.

expected.rationale: The user needs a defensible behavioral review across state owners and entry points, including a verification design. Browser work is not automatically a fixed checklist.

cases.contrastRelation: Counterpart of JVH5-03: identical short request with materially different actual scope.

cases.prompt: Determine which preserved patch contains the missing dialog work and how to restore only that work.

context.originalTask: Independent child: investigate the provided local recovery artifacts and produce a restoration plan. Do not change files or refs.

evidence.text: There are two exported patches and a detached snapshot. Patch A was created before a rebase and includes the dialog plus unrelated navigation changes. Patch B was generated after the rebase and contains only part of the dialog work. The detached snapshot includes uncommitted fixes absent from both patches.

The current checkout already contains a newer navigation implementation and unrelated dirty edits. Several dialog paths were renamed during the rebase. Applying either patch wholesale would overwrite current work.

Compare content and path history, identify which hunks belong to the missing dialog behavior, and give a recoverable ordered plan with evidence. Mark ambiguities explicitly. The child has the artifact paths and checkout, but inherits no chat history.

expected.rationale: The child must reconstruct semantic work across overlapping artifacts while preserving unrelated current changes. Read-only planning still demands careful attribution and ordering.
